question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s consolidated grip on the Chinese Communist Party, military, and state institutions underpins the 95.8% trader consensus that he will remain in power through the end of 2026. At age 73, he shows no public signs of stepping aside, continues to direct policy on the 15th Five-Year Plan and foreign affairs, and has overseen personnel purges that analysts view as reinforcing loyalty rather than signaling weakness. The 21st Party Congress, expected in late 2027, is widely anticipated as the venue for securing a fourth term rather than a transition. While sudden health developments or an unforeseen internal crisis could still alter this trajectory before the market resolves on December 30, 2026, current evidence from official proceedings and leadership positioning indicates few near-term barriers to continuity.
